subject.title: feat(cron): shell precheck gate to skip LLM when no work

question: Should OpenClaw core publish a persisted arbitrary host-shell `job.precheck` contract for cron jobs, including the proposed exit/stdout/error controls, rather than keep the existing trigger and script surfaces as the supported automation boundary?
rationale: The patch is additive and appears to reuse the governed execution policy, but it creates a permanent core scheduler and Gateway protocol API with security and operator implications that code review cannot resolve without product ownership.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core precheck contract
options.body: Approve a small persisted precheck API with the existing policy gates and require Gateway-level proof before merge; defer extra controls and statistics unless they are explicitly needed.

options.title: Accept the full proposed contract
options.body: Adopt all proposed exit-code, stdout-prefix, error-mode, CLI, protocol, and statistics surfaces as the supported cron API.

options.title: Keep shell gating outside this core contract
options.body: Decline the new persisted host-shell precheck API and direct the use case to existing cron trigger or script mechanisms until a narrower core need is established.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core precheck contract
recommendation.body: Approve a small persisted precheck API with the existing policy gates and require Gateway-level proof before merge; defer extra controls and statistics unless they are explicitly needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work spans the cron service and Gateway protocol surfaces that would own this durable core contract.
